HEEWON WEBTOON — bold Korean webtoon / manhwa key art, the finish of a top-tier serialised webtoon cover (Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader, Nano Machine). A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). MEDIUM CLOSE SHOT of ONE character — waist-up or seated — the face large, placed off-centre on a third with breathing room on the side they look toward, from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye or over-the-shoulder), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. LINE: THICK, confident black ink contours with real line weight — a heavy tapered outline around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands; solid black spot-blacks fill the deepest shadows, the hair masses and the insides of sleeves. SHADING: cel-shaded in hard-edged shapes — a base tone, ONE crisp shadow shape and one small sharp highlight per surface, at most one soft gradient for form; glossy graphic highlights on hair, eyes, lacquer and steel. Clean saturated colour. NOT painterly brushwork, NOT watercolor, NOT soft sketchy lines, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. CHARACTER DESIGN: a DESIGNED character, never a generic handsome manhwa face — the face shape, eye shape, brows, nose, mouth, build and posture below belong to this person and no one else, pushed far enough that they read at thumbnail size and in silhouette alone. KOREAN FACES: these are 7th-century Koreans, drawn the way the best Korean webtoons draw Koreans — East Asian bone structure, single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, a low soft nasal bridge, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair; varied from person to person (moon faces, long faces, square jaws), never Western, Latin or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes, never the interchangeable pretty anime face. Keep identity from the attached sheet (hair, dress, colours, ornaments) but REDRAW the person in this bolder style; the sheet's soft sketchy rendering is not the style. INTRODUCING GYEBEK, twenty-one, the boy with the borrowed name, grown — he still cannot say a thing he does not believe. Dawn on the misty river below Sabi, the morning of the king's omen. Low three-quarter angle from beside him on the riverbank: he stands at the king's side (only an out-of-focus crimson royal sleeve at the frame edge), turned half toward the camera, one hand resting on the ring pommel of the sheathed sword at his hip, the other pointing flatly out at the river, where four lacquered paper kites tied nose-to-tail as a 'dragon' float in the mist — plainly paper and bamboo, the strings visible. A heavy deadpan scowl, narrow eyes, utterly literal and unimpressed: "…Your Majesty. That is not a dragon." A low sunrise shaft rakes across his face from the side in hard gold (#d9b13a). Behind him, painted loosely: rose-gold river mist, boats and a far bank of kneeling crowds as soft shapes, banners as bokeh. CHARACTER SHEET (copy this face, hair and clothes exactly): the sheet shows GYEBEK; its bottom row is the only sword design. GYEBEK — Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Colour #d9b13a. DESIGN HOOKS for GYEBEK: gaunt and wiry: a long narrow face, hollow cheeks under high knife-edge cheekbones, narrow single-lidded eyes always half in shadow, straight heavy brows pulled together, thin lips pressed into a flat line, weathered sun-dark skin, a thin pale scar along the left jaw; a few loose strands cut across the brow; the crimson scarf knot is the one bright shape on him. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. BACKGROUND: the real place and moment of the scene simplified into big graphic shapes — two or three flat value planes, a gradient sky or smoke, a few crisp architectural silhouettes, clean circular bokeh lights; background lines thinner and lighter than the figure so the inked character pops forward. LIGHT: ONE hard key light from the place throws a crisp cast-shadow shape across the face and lays a thin bright rim line along the silhouette; the character's colour lives in that light, never a glow aura or halo. ACTING: big readable manhwa expression and body language carrying the line they are about to say. Face and clothes from the sheet; a new pose, never the sheet's stance. ONLY THIS ONE PERSON is the subject — anyone else is at most a dark out-of-focus shape at the frame edge, in period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang or Yamato), never European dress. The quoted line is acting direction only: never letter it, no words or sound effects anywhere. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
